image_prompt.text: A lobby where the whole server gathers before the match and returns between rounds, sized for peak concurrency and open enough that nobody jams at the exits
Transport pads in the lobby that send everyone into the arena when a match starts, and matching pads in the arena that return them when the round ends
A prominent wall in the lobby sized to carry the point standings
An out-of-play strip at the edge of the arena where players who are done with a mini-game wait and watch the rest of the round
A shop in the lobby that players walk into to spend their coins on auras
Several distinct arcade-themed mini-game areas laid out around the arena floor, each one its own recognisable play space

layout_placement.text: Detection regions in each mini-game that register a point when a player finishes it
Evenly distributed start points in the lobby where players join, and in the arena so no player starts a mini-game at an advantage
The markers that move everyone from the lobby into the arena at match start and back to the lobby at round end
The standings surface in the lobby, driven by the points players bank during the round

mechanics: players get more points per mini game they finish
whoever has the most points wins the round
the round winner is awarded some coins
coins are spent at the shop in the lobby
matches run back to back — once one match finishes another starts
players spawn in the lobby before the match
notes: Preset Minigame taken whole, on its own shape space-staged. Added social-hub (the prompt names a lobby), spawn-protected (the prompt names where players spawn twice) and building-interior (the lobby shop).

P4 comes from space-staged plus teleporter-link read as a portal to a separate place: the prompt spawns players out of the lobby into the arena rather than walking them there. P3 comes from the lobby shop. Neither route is available today; both are recorded rather than downgraded because the prompt states the feature.

The round's terminus is the return teleport to the lobby plus the standings wall, inferred from the genre and preset rather than stated. No winner-zone: the payoff the prompt names is coins, which is progression.

The arena is arcade-themed — should the lobby match it (neon, cabinets, carpet, ticket counter), or read as a plainer neutral waiting area?

skill_gap.name: shape display name not in genre file
skill_gap.why: Step 6 requires shape.type and shape.name split from the shape row's **Type (Flavor Name)**, but a genre file only carries that split for shapes it rewords in its own table. Party & Casual reworks space-bounded and not space-staged, so the preset's own shape cannot be emitted in full without reading shapes.md — which step 2 and the read scope both say not to open when the typical shapes fit. Emitted type and name as null.

notes_for_us: The one shape the Minigame preset names cannot be emitted from the genre file alone: only rewritten shapes carry the Type (Flavor Name) split that step 6 demands. Every genre file has this hole for its non-reworded typical shapes.

Step 2's ordered search says a costume shop is building-interior, which forces P3; step 4 says prefer P0/P6 when nothing requires a modifier and read for the feature rather than the keyword. A lobby shop in a Roblox party game is usually a stall with a GUI, so the two rules point opposite ways and nothing arbitrates.

A multi-minigame arena has no option anywhere in the catalogue — space-staged says the round is staged elsewhere but nothing holds 'and there are several different games in it'. It went out as free text, which drops any route it would have carried.

Nothing in the network takes a screen-space request. The shop's buying interface is plainly a GUI, so it was either forced into a layout entry or dropped; it is logged as a ui destination only because the eval record has that field, not because the skills do.

spectator-zone is *varies* in options.md but flat in Party & Casual's own table, and the preset ships it. Neither file says which route a preset-derived spectator area takes when the prompt never mentions spectating.
